newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt wants extension of emergency law.
newsitem.headline: Egypt wants extension of emergency law.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri asked parliament on Sunday to approve a presidential decree to extend for another three years emergency law, in force since President Anwar Sadat was assassinated in 1981.

Ganzouri justified the extension as protection for Egypt's expanding economy from sabotage by "terrorists", the government's term for Moslem militants fighting to turn Egypt into a purist Islamic state.

"We only see terrorists in countries that are rapidly developing and not in countries that are poor. Our economy is fast becoming international and the forces of evil have moved to stop the flood of investments in Egypt," he said.

Ganzouri said that the militants, fighting since 1992, had last tried scare off the mainly Western investors against coming to Egypt when the militants killed 10 Christian youths in a south Egyptian church on February 12.
Police are still searching for the suspected Islamist gunmen who stormed the church.
"First, they tried to hit our tourism industry and now they are sending a message to the Christian west that there is no security in Egypt," Ganzouri added.

Moslem militants have often targeted tourists, Christians and government officials in their campaign to topple the government. More than 1,000 people have died in the five years of political violence.

Emergency law has been in place in Egypt since Moslem militant gunmen shot dead Sadat at a military parade in 1981. Parliament has extended it regularly ever since, despite protests by leftist and liberal opposition groups.
Emergency law enables the authorities to hold detainees without charges for long periods and to try civilians in military courts, where defendants have fewer rights.
Parliament is expected to vote on extending emergency law later on Sunday or on Monday.
